items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1963-03-29
items.q: Leo Daniel, that was my brother. The first band we had together was the Moonlight Serenade.

ctx.x: And Leo, he wasn't much of a street man.

Leo was a good street man at the time because the brass band he played with had the music, you see, and he could read anything they put up there. And that's why Shawnee Neen was crazy about him. But he didn't play too much brass band work. Mostly he played like with Shawnee Neen, you know, and brass bands like that. He did most of the orchestra work, played with Pierron, you know, and had the band they made up around there, the band there. And he played with Rizzly Tuxedo when I was playing with him. And he…
Well, what trumpet player plays Sid now, much which or not?

items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: I said, listen, my little brother. I told Leo, I said, that's your thing out of it.

ctx.x: Yeah, he don't like to get off like that, but he can get off. He don't like to get off.

You know what he does? He proved, you know Leo surprised me, the first time he surprised me when he was playing with the Sonny South. The South man, that's right. They had a contest on the roof garden there, six bands, no, no, four bands. And they used to play . And Alvin McNeil, who's a new player himself, always wanted to play that trumpet solo. And ring that bell, so Leo said, too many bands have been nice. I already played dancing, I don't think you should play that. He said, I'm a player. So Leo played that…

items.title: Fred Minor Interview, 1961-11-01
items.q: Me, Emma, Barry, Gilbert, Young, my brother Leo, and this trombone player I was telling you about that stayed dressed up all the time.

ctx.x: So I wondered, because some people said, oh, they called one the society band. Like these people.

But here's what they must have been thinking about, you see. You see, when Salisand Ridley broke up, we had Riznitz tuxedo, and Salisand's tuxedo, you see, because I was on the road with Riznitz tuxedo in the 20s. Yeah, that may be what I heard then. Yeah, that's what I heard. Me, Emma, Barry, Gilbert, Young, my brother Leo, and this trombone player I was telling you about that stayed dressed up all the time. We all changed clothes, you know, right on the road, and he'd stay dressed up just in his tuxedo suit.…
That's how he did it. Yeah, it's hard to do.
